statement: A governmental entity acting under § 2703 may apply to a court for an order commanding a provider to whom a warrant, subpoena, or court order is directed not to notify any other person of the demand's existence, for such period as the court deems appropriate; the court shall enter the order on finding reason to believe that notification will result in one of the enumerated harms, such as endangering a person, flight from prosecution, evidence destruction, witness intimidation, or seriously jeopardizing an investigation (18 U.S.C. § 2705(b)).
caveat: Absent a § 2705(b) order or another sealing obligation, the statute does not itself forbid the recipient from notifying the affected user; contractual terms, other statutes, and the demand's own wording can. Whether and when to notify is a counsel determination. This repo does not interpret gag orders.
